target_subject: a lion and a human figure standing side by side

scene: A high-contrast black-and-white ink drawing featuring a large lion on the left and a muscular human figure on the right, both facing forward.
The background is minimally rendered with loose sketch lines suggesting open space or indistinct terrain.
The composition is frontal and symmetrical in balance, with the lion occupying roughly two-thirds of the left visual field.
action: The lion stands upright on all four paws, head raised, mouth closed, gaze directed forward.
The human figure holds a sword aloft in the right hand and grips a shield with the left hand, positioned in front of the torso.
The human figure’s left leg is forward, right leg back, suggesting a static combat-ready stance.
rationale: The lion’s posture and facial expression suggest alertness rather than aggression, based on relaxed jaw and open eyes without bared teeth.
The human figure appears to be armored partially—visible chest plate and greaves—but lacks full coverage; this may indicate stylized representation rather than historical accuracy.
The shield bears an emblem that resembles a stylized animal head or mask, but details are too ambiguous to identify definitively.
object: The lion has a full, flowing mane rendered with dense cross-hatching and varied line weight, covering its neck and shoulders.
The human figure has long hair and a full beard, both depicted with textured shading and directional strokes.
The sword has a straight double-edged blade and a simple hilt with a rounded pommel; no guard detail is clearly visible.
The shield is kite-shaped with a central boss and a darkened emblem consisting of curved and angular forms.
The human wears a sleeveless tunic over what appears to be a cuirass, with articulated greaves on both lower legs and a sash or strap crossing the torso.

sword-and-shield as instruments of deliberate defense

alternative_interpretations: This may simply depict a mythological pairing (e.g., hero and companion beast) without deeper intent, common in heraldic or allegorical illustration.
limitations: No textual labels or contextual setting confirm symbolic intent; the image alone does not establish normative claims about responsibility.
